summary.text: A wave-cut platform is a narrow, flat area at the base of a sea cliff or along the shore of a lake, bay or sea, created by erosion.
Waves cut a notch between the high and low water marks, the notch grows into a cave, and when the cave roof collapses the cliff retreats and the cave floor is left as the platform.
Raised, abandoned platforms record higher sea levels of the past and help measure how fast land is rising now that it is no longer under ice.

facts.label: Best seen
facts.value: At low tide, as huge areas of flat rock

facts.value: Between the high and low water marks

items.prompt: Waves start attacking the foot of a fresh, vertical sea cliff. What forms there before anything else?

options.label: A flat shelf of bare rock
A notch undercutting the base
A heap of fallen roof rock
A beach just offshore

items.explain: Waves first undercut the cliff between high and low water, making a notch; the notch becomes a cave, whose roof later collapses.

items.prompt: You want to walk out across a wide, flat rock shelf left behind by a retreating cliff. When are you most likely to see it best?

options.label: At high tide, when waves are biggest
Right after sand has piled up on it
Only from a boat far out at sea
At low tide, when the water drops

items.explain: These platforms are most obvious at low tide, when they show as large areas of flat rock; sand can hide them otherwise.

items.prompt: Hikers find a flat rock shelf with marine fossils, sitting well above and behind today's beach. What does it most likely tell geologists?

options.label: A storm once threw the rock up there
People built it as an old quay
The sea once stood higher against that land
The rock slowly grew up from the beach

items.explain: Raised, abandoned platforms behind modern beaches are evidence of higher sea levels in the past, and their fossils help date them.

items.prompt: A coastline has been jolted upward by several earthquakes over thousands of years. What might you find along it?

options.label: A series of flat shelves at different heights
One single shelf that has sunk underwater
No shelves, as quakes erase all of them
Deep caves but never any flat shelves

items.explain: Where seismic action changes the coast, a series of platforms can show earlier sea levels and how much each earthquake lifted the land.

items.prompt: Rock pools on these flat shelves hold far fewer kinds of creatures than you might expect. What makes it such a tough home?

options.label: Deep shade cast by the cliff
The relentless pounding of waves
Water that is too fresh to live in
Rock that releases poisonous gas

items.explain: Continual wave action makes the platform an extremely hostile environment that only certain organisms can use.

items.prompt: Some coastal scientists argue the name 'wave-cut platform' should be dropped in favor of 'shore platform'. Why?

options.label: The surfaces are rarely flat in practice
They form only on lakes, never seas
The name is easy to confuse with beaches
It assumes a cause that is not always true

items.explain: The old name assumes these platforms are made by wave action, which is not always the case.
